column1: enrolment|The process of joining a course or institution.|Online enrolment closes three days before the course starts.
enrol|To register officially for a course.|You can enrol at the college reception desk.
registration|The recording of someone's details for an activity or service.|Bring photo identification to complete registration.
admission|Permission to enter an institution or course.|Admission depends on your previous study and language skills.
entry requirement|A condition that must be met before joining a course.|The main entry requirement is a basic computer certificate.
funding|Money provided to support an activity.|The centre has secured funding for evening classes.
grant|Money given for a particular purpose, usually without repayment.|The training grant pays for essential equipment.
student|Someone who is studying.|Each student receives access to the online library.
learner|Someone developing knowledge or a skill.|The course is suitable for an adult learner returning to study.
tutor|A teacher who supports a small group or individual.|Contact your tutor if you need help with the assignment.
lecturer|Someone who teaches at a college or university.|The lecturer will explain how to prepare for the assessment.
instructor|Someone who teaches a practical skill.|Follow the instructor's demonstration before using the machine.
mentor|An experienced person who advises and supports someone.|Your mentor will help you plan your development.
classroom|A room where teaching takes place.|The classroom is on the ground floor.
lecture|A teaching session in which someone explains a subject.|The introductory lecture is available as a recording.
seminar|A small teaching session involving discussion.|Prepare two questions for the next seminar.
workshop|A practical session for learning or developing skills.|The workshop teaches basic bicycle maintenance.
tutorial|A teaching session for an individual or small group.|Book a tutorial if you need extra writing support.
course|A series of lessons on a subject.|The evening course runs for ten weeks.
module|One complete part of a larger course.|You must finish the safety module before practical training.
syllabus|A list of the subjects covered by a course.|The syllabus includes customer care and business communication.
term|One of the periods into which a teaching year is divided.|The new term begins on Monday.
semester|One of two main teaching periods in a year.|You can choose an optional subject next semester.
timetable|A list showing when classes or events take place.|Check the timetable for your classroom number.
lesson|A period of teaching on a subject.|The first lesson covers safe use of hand tools.
assignment|A piece of work set for a learner to complete.|Submit your assignment through the student website.
assessment|A process of judging someone's knowledge or skills.|The assessment includes a written test and a demonstration.
examination|A formal test of knowledge or ability.|Bring your identification to the examination room.
quiz|A short test of knowledge.|The tutor starts each session with a short quiz.
certificate|A document confirming an achievement or completion.|You receive a certificate after completing the course.
diploma|A qualification awarded after a course of study.|The diploma includes a supervised work placement.
degree|A qualification awarded by a university.|Her degree helped her apply for the management programme.
placement|A temporary position that provides practical experience.|The college arranges a placement with a local employer.
practical|Involving doing something rather than only learning theory.|Wear suitable clothing for the practical session.
theory|Ideas or principles that explain how something works.|The course combines theory with supervised practice.
foundation|A basic level of study that prepares learners for further work.|The foundation course develops essential language skills.
intermediate|Between a basic and an advanced level.|The intermediate class is for learners with some experience.
advanced|At a high level of knowledge or skill.|The advanced workshop requires previous training.
optional|Available as a choice rather than a requirement.|The weekend field trip is optional.
grade|A mark or level showing the quality of work.|Your final grade includes the practical assessment.
pass|To achieve the required standard in a test.|You must pass the safety test before using the workshop.
resit|To take an examination again.|Students who are unsuccessful may resit the test in July.
revision|Review of material already learned before a test.|The tutor has prepared a revision guide.
revise|To review material in preparation for a test.|Use the practice questions to revise before Friday.
practise|To repeat an activity to improve a skill.|You can practise your interview answers with a partner.
progress|Improvement or movement towards a goal.|Your tutor will discuss your progress each month.
achievement|Something successfully completed through effort.|Finishing the course was an important achievement for her.
objective|A specific result that someone aims to achieve.|The main objective is to improve workplace communication.
outcome|The result of an activity or process.|A key learning outcome is the ability to write clear instructions.
fluency|The ability to speak or write smoothly.|Regular conversation practice can improve fluency.
accuracy|The quality of being correct and precise.|The exercise checks accuracy when entering customer details.
pronunciation|The way a word is spoken.|Listen to the recording to check pronunciation.
vocabulary|The words someone knows or uses.|The course develops vocabulary for everyday services.
grammar|The rules used to form words and sentences.|This lesson reviews grammar for writing formal requests.
comprehension|The ability to understand what you read or hear.|The worksheet checks comprehension of a staff notice.
explanation|Information that makes something easier to understand.|Ask for an explanation if the instructions are unclear.
example|A specific case that helps explain an idea.|The teacher gave an example of a polite complaint.
exercise|An activity designed to develop or check a skill.|Complete the listening exercise before the next class.
textbook|A book used for studying a subject.|You can borrow the textbook from the library.
workbook|A book containing practice activities.|Bring your workbook to every practical session.
notebook|A book of blank pages for writing notes.|Keep useful phrases in a small notebook.
stationery|Materials such as paper, pens and envelopes.|Basic stationery is included in the course fee.
resource|Something useful for learning or completing a task.|The online dictionary is a useful learning resource.
reference book|A book consulted for particular information.|This reference book must remain in the library.
research|Careful investigation to find information or answers.|Your project requires research into local transport needs.
source|A place from which information is obtained.|Name the source of each statistic in your report.
summary|A short account of the main points.|Write a summary of the safety instructions.
essay|A structured piece of writing discussing a topic.|The essay should explain both benefits and disadvantages.
paragraph|A group of sentences dealing with one main idea.|Start a new paragraph when introducing another reason.
draft|An early version of a piece of work.|Bring your first draft to the tutorial.
proofread|To check writing for errors before finishing it.|Please proofread the application before sending it.
submit|To hand in work for checking or consideration.|Submit the completed worksheet by email.
extension|Extra time allowed to complete something.|Ask for an extension before the assignment is due.
withdraw|To leave a course or remove an application formally.|Contact student services if you need to withdraw.
transfer|To move from one course, place or system to another.|You can transfer to the evening class if space is available.
attendance record|A written account of the sessions someone attended.|Keep your attendance record for the final assessment.
learning support|Help provided to make studying easier.|Contact learning support to arrange accessible materials.
distance learning|Study completed away from a classroom using remote materials.|Distance learning lets her study around her work schedule.
self-paced|Completed at a speed chosen by the learner.|The online module is self-paced but has a final deadline.
lifelong learning|Continuing to develop knowledge and skills throughout life.|The community centre encourages lifelong learning through evening classes.
prerequisite|Something required before another activity can begin.|A first-aid certificate is a prerequisite for the placement.
tuition|Teaching or the charge made for teaching.|The grant covers tuition but not travel expenses.
scholarship|Money awarded to help someone pay for study.|The scholarship is available to local adult learners.
bursary|Financial support given to a student who needs it.|Apply for a bursary if you cannot afford course materials.
curriculum|The overall programme of study at an institution.|Practical skills are central to the college curriculum.
apprenticeship|Training that combines paid work with study.|The apprenticeship includes one college day each week.
traineeship|A period of practical training for a job.|The traineeship introduces learners to office administration.
internship|A short period of work intended to develop experience.|The internship offers experience in community services.
vocational|Related to skills for a particular occupation.|The college provides vocational courses in catering.
compulsory|Required by a rule.|Attendance at the induction session is compulsory.
elective|A subject that a learner chooses to study.|You may take photography as an elective.
course credit|A unit recognising completed study.|This module counts towards the course credit needed for your diploma.
transcript|An official record of subjects studied and results.|Send a copy of your transcript with the application.
literacy|The ability to read and write.|The centre offers free adult literacy classes.
numeracy|The ability to understand and use numbers.|Basic numeracy is needed for the bookkeeping course.
citation|A reference showing where information came from.|Include a citation when quoting the article.
plagiarism|Presenting someone else's work as your own.|The college has clear rules against plagiarism.
defer|To delay starting something until a later date.|You may defer your place until next term.
recognition|Official acceptance of an achievement or qualification.|Ask whether the certificate has recognition among local employers.
accreditation|Official approval that a course meets required standards.|The training provider has national accreditation.
